jobs.description: At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us. Corporate Audit Services Organization Overview Corporate Audit Services (CAS) is an independent, objective audit and consulting function driven by a commitment to add value and enhance the operations of Eli Lilly and Company. CAS's mission is to support the company in achieving its objectives by employing a systematic, disciplined approach to evaluate and improve the effectiveness of risk management, control, and governance processes. Position Description This position builds and delivers best-in-class, end-to-end analytics solutions on Microsoft Fabric, the foundation of the CAS data platform. Working across the full lifecycle, from data engineering, warehousing, and ELT through semantic models, Power BI, and Fabric apps, the individual creates and evolves a portfolio of Fabric solutions that turn CAS data into trusted, self-service intelligence. A core focus is building AI Ready Semantic Models, the governed, contextual data layer that grounds Claude and AI agents in trusted CAS data. Partnering directly with CAS audit teams and stakeholders, the individual translates business needs into working solutions, drives efforts to completion, and grows adoption across the function, delivering high-quality, well-governed solutions within the CAS data architecture and data engine standards. The individual also helps innovate how CAS builds and automates, leveraging Claude Code and beginning to apply agentic frameworks to accelerate development and automate CAS audit and Data Analytics operations. Above all, this is a hands-on builder who thrives on a team of doers, collaborates openly, sets and evolves standards alongside peers, and partners across Finance and the broader Lilly organization to deliver where it creates the most value. Success in this role is as much about how the work gets done as what gets built. This is a highly collaborative, hands-on team of builders who share openly, support one another, and put the team's success first. The individual brings an ownership mindset and a high personal bar, communicates with clarity and empathy, stays humble and curious, and builds trust across CAS and its partners, contributing to a positive culture where people do their best work. Primary Position Responsibilities Fabric Data Engineering & ELT Design, build, and maintain scalable data solutions on Microsoft Fabric, spanning lakehouses, warehouses, and a medallion architecture (Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers). Engineer the full ELT lifecycle, building ingestion, transformation, and refresh pipelines with Fabric notebooks and configuration-driven frameworks that are scalable, reusable, and maintainable. Build and maintain data orchestration across solutions, coordinating pipelines, dependencies, scheduling, and refresh. Refactor and migrate existing solutions onto the Fabric platform, following established governance and deployment standards. Apply CI/CD, Git version control, and automated testing that bring engineering rigor and repeatability to solution development. Uphold and extend the CAS data architecture and governance frameworks, keeping solutions secure, well-structured, and maintainable at enterprise scale. Semantic Models, Power BI & Fabric Apps Build data engines and semantic models on Fabric to the CAS data engine standards, primarily using Direct Lake, with strong attention to DAX and model performance for governed, high-performance consumption by Power BI, Fabric apps, and Claude. Develop AI Ready Semantic Models, establishing the holistic contextual layer within the semantic model (definitions, relationships, and business meaning) that makes it consumable by large language models and grounds Claude in trusted CAS data. Leverage Claude, MCP, and Claude Code to build and enrich AI Ready Semantic Models and to innovate how CAS delivers AI-grounded analytics. Own Power BI solution delivery, building dashboards, executive visualizations, and reporting that make data accessible and actionable for stakeholders. Innovate new Fabric app solutions, designing and building Fabric-native applications that extend how CAS delivers and consumes data. Architect self-service analytics that enable stakeholders to explore data without ongoing developer support. Establish enterprise deployment patterns, including shared datasets, deployment pipelines, and version control that bring engineering rigor to analytics delivery. Solution Delivery & Stakeholder Partnership Partner with CAS audit leadership to understand their priorities, workflows, and process pain points, translating them into analytics and automation solutions that measurably improve how audits are executed. Act as a trusted advisor, proactively identifying opportunities to streamline audit processes and bringing forward solutions rather than waiting for requirements. Maintain and evolve a portfolio of Fabric solutions, continuously improving performance, usability, and reliability. Deliver organizational reporting and analytics dashboards for business partners, leaders, and stakeholders. Orchestrate work delivery through Smartsheet, managing intake, prioritization, tracking, and delivery metrics. Operate in an Agile delivery model, driving continuous improvement, adoption, and business value. Automation & Agentic Innovation Automate CAS audit processes, building automation solutions for auditors that reduce manual effort and improve consistency across audit execution. Automate Data Analytics operations, streamlining intake, delivery, and platform tasks to increase team efficiency and quality. Leverage Claude Code and AI-assisted development to accelerate the build and maintenance of Fabric and automation solutions. Pilot autonomous solutioning, applying agentic frameworks to automate build, testing, and operational tasks as this emerging capability matures. Contribute to the CAS Claude Skill strategy, helping create and maintain reusable skills that encode Fabric, solution, and automation capabilities. Pioneer and help define how agentic approaches evolve into AI-native CAS solutions over time, establishing early patterns the team will build on. Technical Leadership & Innovation Set, follow, and evolve technical standards alongside the team, contributing best practices, design patterns, and reusable templates to the shared Confluence repository referenced across Data Analytics and CAS. Lead solution design for complex analytics and data challenges, shaping the approach and bringing peers along collaboratively. Own delivery end to end, driving efforts to completion and taking accountability for quality, performance, and outcomes. Contribute to solution and code reviews, exchanging feedback with peers to keep quality, consistency, and governance high across the team. Advance how CAS builds, evaluating and piloting emerging Fabric, analytics, and agentic capabilities and sharing what works so the whole team benefits. Share knowledge and enablement, helping build collective capability on Fabric, semantic modeling, Power BI, and AI tools. Basic Qualifications / Requirements Bachelor's Degree in Business Analytics, Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, or related technical degree. 5+ years of relevant professional experience in data engineering, analytics, or data solution development within a global, matrixed organization. Additional Skills / Preferences Demonstrated experience leading end-to-end data solution delivery and setting technical standards that others follow, including through solution and design reviews. Drive root-cause analysis and resolution of optical issues, including reflections, glare, Mura, halo artifacts, Newton Rings, and coating non-uniformity. Collaborate with suppliers to validate technologies under automotive environmental and reliability conditions. Build technology maturation packages and support technology transfer into future sourcing and production programs. Familiarity with optical performance metrics such as luminance, contrast, haze, reflectivity, color shift, and viewing angle. POSITION SUMMARY
This role provides actuarial support for Bermuda Economic Balance Sheet (EBS) valuation and leads key components of new reinsurance deal onboarding. Responsibilities include model development, data integration, financial reporting support, and coordination across actuarial, pricing, and technology teams. The position ensures accurate, efficient, and well-controlled actuarial processes that meet regulatory and organizational standards.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Bermuda EBS Modeling & Valuation Support
Lead the development, enhancement, and maintenance of actuarial models used for Bermuda EBS valuation, working in close partnership with the Bermuda Actuarial team.
Support assumption updates, model changes, and process improvements to strengthen reporting accuracy and efficiency.
Assist with data integration workflows, including ETL processes and validation routines, to ensure reliable data for valuation.
Participate in cash flow model development and valuation testing activities.
Help resolve issues arising during production cycles by collaborating with cross-functional partners.
Prepare documentation and testing materials to comply with internal governance and regulatory expectations.
Reinsurance Deal Onboarding
Partner with the pricing team to transfer knowledge, assumptions, and methodologies for new reinsurance transactions.
Ensure valuation model readiness by assisting with feature development and pricing-to-valuation model alignment.
Support interim financial reporting using pricing models until valuation model components are finalized.
Participate in data onboarding automation, including mapping, validation, and control processes to enable scalable new-deal integration.
Collaboration & Communication
Work closely with actuarial, pricing, data, reporting, and technology teams to support both ongoing valuation and new business initiatives.
Communicate technical findings, issues, and recommendations in a clear and structured manner.
Spearhead the communication of commercial updates to the actuarial and related functions through active partnership with the Commercial team.
Identify and scale solutions developed for Bermuda and Deal onboarding for other modeling needs.
QUALIFICATIONS
Strong technical actuarial and analytical skills and foundational actuarial modeling experience.
Embraces using new and emerging technology and experimentation
Specific technical skills preferred:
Model design, control and governance best practices
Asset-liability modeling techniques
Knowledge of US life and annuity products and their features (e.g. FA, FIA, VA, RILA, payout/SPIA, PRT, UL, VUL, IUL)
US GAAP, Bermuda EBS and US statutory valuation principles and methods
Ability to work collaboratively across functions and manage multiple priorities.
Familiarity with actuarial systems, valuation processes, and data workflows.
Demonstrates exceptional client service focus.
Actuarial fellowship designation required.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic's Integrity & Compliance (I&C) function is building the systems that let us scale responsibly as our products reach more people, more enterprises, and more regulated industries. Our global compliance program is bespoke, reflecting our unique mission and position as one of the leading AI labs operating on the frontier.
Our Regulatory Programs pillar is a key pillar of our overall Integrity & Compliance function and covers a range of compliance domain areas including economic sanctions, US export controls, and regulatory compliance programs stemming from global content and AI regulation.
As Sanctions Compliance Lead, you will take day-to-day leadership of Anthropic's sanctions compliance program and support oversight of our export controls program, supporting the Regulatory Programs lead as a senior leader within the function. This is a leadership seat in a domain where the rules governing AI models and compute are still being written, and where sanctions exposure runs through globally accessible APIs, downstream and embedded-partner channels, and rapid geographic expansion.
You will own the sanctions program end to end: setting strategy and risk appetite with leadership, continuously assessing risk and driving remediation and program enhancements, governing our screening and enforcement controls, directing regulator-facing matters, and reporting on program health to I&C leadership and the Audit Committee. You will partner closely with our in-house Trade Compliance Counsel on interpretation of applicable law, represent the function with senior stakeholders, and lead and develop trade compliance professionals as the team grows. This is a builder's role at a company that takes integrity seriously and moves fast. You will exercise independent judgment on issues without clear precedent and build durable programs that let Anthropic move quickly while honoring its obligations to regulators, customers, and the public.
Key responsibilities
Lead Anthropic's sanctions compliance program, including strategy, risk appetite, policy frameworks, and the program roadmap, and keep them current as regulations and the business evolve
Represent the sanctions and export controls function with senior leadership and cross-functional partners, and step in for the Regulatory Programs lead across the function as needed
Continuously assess sanctions risk across products, channels, and markets, and own the remediation of identified issues and the delivery of program enhancements, in partnership with Legal, Internal Audit, Finance, and first-line teams
Direct regulator-facing matters, including voluntary self-disclosures, blocking and reject reports, licensing questions, and responses to regulator or third-party inquiries, in partnership with Trade Compliance Counsel and National Security Legal
Govern Anthropic's restricted-party screening and enforcement controls, including list configuration, thresholds, escalation criteria, vendor management, and exception review, in partnership with Regulatory Operations and Safeguards
Serve as the senior escalation point for complex sanctions matters surfaced by Safeguards, Threat Intelligence, Go-to-Market, and Finance, and set the standards by which first-line teams disposition and escalate cases
Advise business and product teams on sanctions and trade controls implications of commercial and geographic expansion, new products and channels, partnerships, and acquisitions, and translate findings into clear control requirements
Support oversight of the export controls program, partnering with the Sanctions & Export Controls Compliance Officer and Trade Compliance Counsel on program priorities, controls, and reporting
Prepare and deliver program reporting on health, key risks, and emerging issues for I&C and Legal leadership, the Audit Committee, and other governance forums
Monitor sanctions regulatory developments and enforcement actions, assess impact on Anthropic, and drive required program changes
Lead, mentor, and develop compliance team members, and help shape the structure of the function as it grows
Of course, this is just a sample of the kinds of work this role will require! You should assume that your role will encompass other tasks, too, and that your job duties and responsibilities may change from time to time at Anthropic's discretion, or otherwise applicable with local law
Minimum qualifications
Substantive, hands-on experience leading an economic sanctions compliance program (OFAC, EU, UK, and other applicable regimes) in a commercial environment, including program design, policy ownership, and risk governance
Experience managing voluntary self-disclosures, blocking or reject reports, and other regulator filings end to end, including coordinating counsel, internal stakeholders, and remediation
Experience assessing sanctions risk on an ongoing basis and owning the remediation of identified issues and delivery of program enhancements through to closure
Experience governing a restricted-party screening program, including list scope, match thresholds, escalation criteria, and screening vendor management
A track record of reporting on program health and risk to senior leadership, an audit committee, or a board, and of driving decisions on risk appetite with executives
Working knowledge of US export controls (EAR and BIS rules) sufficient to oversee an export controls program and partner effectively with technical subject-matter experts
Experience partnering with in-house and outside counsel to interpret trade controls requirements and translating them into practical guidance for product, engineering, operations, and commercial teams
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including drafting policy and preparing materials for senior leadership
Preferred qualifications
10+ years of relevant experience in economic sanctions compliance, including several years leading a program or team
Experience managing and developing compliance professionals
Experience conducting sanctions diligence for acquisitions, vendors, and third parties, including state-ownership and 50 percent rule analysis
Experience partnering with trust and safety, enforcement, or threat intelligence teams on account actions and sanctions escalations
Exposure to sanctions compliance in software, cloud, fintech, or AI contexts, including globally accessible platforms and downstream access risk
Prior experience in a Big 4 or other compliance consulting or advisory professional services firm, or at OFAC or another trade regulator
Experience in a hyper-scaling tech company or other fast-paced environment
Sound judgment and the ability to make risk-based decisions and move work forward with imperfect information
A leadership style characterized by integrity, humility, strategic thinking, and solution-orientation

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit

How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

The Power Generation team is seeking an Electrical Technician to operate and maintain plant electrical systems at SpaceX’s power generation facility. You will work hands-on across medium-voltage generation, distribution, and balance-of-plant electrical equipment up to 13.5 kV and 34.8 kV. This is an operations and maintenance role — you will switch, troubleshoot, repair, and keep electrical systems online in a high-reliability, fast-paced plant environment.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Perform operations and maintenance on plant electrical systems, including generators, transformers, switchgear, motor control centers, motors, VFDs, UPS units, automatic transfer switches, and emergency/black-start equipment, at voltages up to 13.5 kV and 34.8 kV.
Execute switching, isolation, LOTO, racking of breakers, and restoration of medium-voltage equipment in accordance with plant procedures and NFPA 70E.
Troubleshoot electrical faults on power distribution, protection, grounding, lighting, and auxiliary systems using one-line diagrams, schematics, and electrical test equipment.
Perform preventive and predictive maintenance, inspections, and repairs to improve reliability and reduce unplanned downtime.
Support plant startups, shutdowns, outages, and commissioning activities alongside operators, controls technicians, and engineers.
Install, terminate, and maintain plant electrical equipment, cable, and control wiring as required for operations and maintenance work.
Respond to electrical alarms, trips, and equipment failures; support root-cause investigations and implement corrective actions.
Coordinate with operations, engineering, and utility personnel on switching, clearances, and electrical work that affects plant generation.
Maintain accurate work orders, switching records, and as-found/as-left documentation.
Follow all safety, LOTO, arc-flash, and PPE requirements while working in energized and hazardous plant environments.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
High school diploma or equivalency certificate
3+ years of experience as an electrical technician, industrial electrician, or similar role maintaining industrial or power generation electrical systems.
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
Experience operating and maintaining medium-voltage electrical systems (4.16 kV to 34.8 kV), including switchgear, transformers, and breakers.
Experience in a power plant, generating station, or other high-reliability industrial facility.
Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, electrical schematics, and equipment O&M manuals.
Experience with LOTO, switching procedures, and NFPA 70E / arc-flash safety practices.
Experience troubleshooting motors, VFDs, MCCs, UPS systems, and plant auxiliary electrical equipment.
Familiarity with electrical test equipment (multimeters, insulation testers, infrared, and similar).
Journeyman electrician license or equivalent formal electrical training.
Experience using a CMMS or work-order system to plan and close maintenance work.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-discipline operations and maintenance team.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Willingness to perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights.
Ability to work extended hours, nights, weekends, and rotating or on-call schedules to support plant operations.
Ability to remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE.
Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted.
Lifting, standing, climbing, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, stretching, and carrying are generally required to perform the functions of this position.
Must be able to work on-site at the power generation facility, with potential travel to other SpaceX sites.

jobs.description: Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks.
